clue.text: Writer's apostle endlessly featured in Authorised Version

indicators.note: something featured in a work sits inside it, so the shortened name goes inside the version's initials
without an end means the final letter of the apostle's name is lopped off

parts.note: first half of AV, the standard abbreviation for the Authorised Version of the Bible
Simon Peter, or Simon the Zealot, two of the twelve apostles
second half of AV, the Authorised Version

explanation.surface: A religious writer's favourite apostle crops up throughout the King James Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: AV is the usual abbreviation for the Authorised (King James) Version; SIMON minus its last letter sits between the A and the V.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Asimov was a prolific science-fiction author, so he is a writer by profession.

clue.text: Copyist split with European in staff room

indicators.note: in places the preceding words inside the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: SCR is the Senior Common Room, the staff room of a British college
riven is an old past participle meaning split apart
E is the standard abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A clerk who copies documents splits up with a European colleague in the staff room.
explanation.walkthrough: In Oxford and Cambridge colleges the Senior Common Room (SCR) is where the academic staff gather.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrivener was a professional scribe who copied documents by hand before printing and typing.

clue.text: Mixed metaphors in one such as Timon

indicators.note: mixed means jumbled together, so the letters that follow are stirred into a new order

parts.note: the two words as letter material

explanation.surface: A critic complains of mixed metaphors in Shakespeare's Timon of Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: Timon of Athens, in Shakespeare's play, turns bitterly against all humanity after his friends desert him.
explanation.definitionFit: Timon becomes the classic hater of mankind, so he is an example of someone who loathes people.

clue.text: Double check for climbing plant

parts.note: to vet is to check thoroughly; the first of the two checks
ch is the chess abbreviation for check; the second of the two checks

explanation.surface: A gardener double-checks before choosing a climber for the trellis.
explanation.walkthrough: Double check means two words for check side by side: one meaning examine, one the chess abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Vetch is a leguminous plant of the pea family that climbs by tendrils.

clue.text: Jam is essential when making cream tea

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a fix or predicament, trouble one is in
second meaning: literally the boiling liquid you pour on the leaves

explanation.surface: Jam is the essential ingredient of a cream tea, along with scones and clotted cream.
explanation.walkthrough: A cream tea is a British afternoon tea of scones, jam and clotted cream, so jam looks like a food here; it is really a predicament, and the tea itself needs boiling liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in hot water is to be in trouble, just as being in a jam is; and tea cannot be brewed without it.

clue.text: Pointedly secure in Old English, express opinion

indicators.note: in puts the fastening word inside the abbreviation that follows it

parts.note: OE is the standard abbreviation for Old English
to pin something is to fasten it with a sharp point

explanation.surface: A scholar firmly states a view in Old English, as if speaking with conviction.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to state one's view, a formal synonym for giving an opinion.

clue.text: Practise on river in punt

parts.note: to wage war is to carry it on, to practise it
R is the abbreviation for river, placed on (after) the first part in a down clue

explanation.surface: Someone practises on the river in a flat-bottomed boat, as on the Cam.
explanation.walkthrough: Punt suggests the flat boat poled along Cambridge rivers; it is also a bet, a punter being a gambler.
explanation.definitionFit: A punt is a stake laid on a horse or game, so it is a bet.

clue.text: Digit hit at the end becoming black

indicators.note: becoming at the end means the final letter is swapped for the one named next

parts.note: to thump is to hit hard
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A finger is struck so hard at the tip that it turns black.
explanation.walkthrough: The P that ends THUMP is replaced by B.
explanation.definitionFit: The thumb is one of the five digits of the hand.

clue.text: Woman tempted to devour Whopper after dinner ultimately finds comfort

indicators.note: ultimately means at the last, so only the final letter of the meal is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

indicators.note: to devour is to take something inside, so the woman's name swallows the falsehood

parts.note: Eve was tempted by the serpent in Eden
a whopper is a big lie

explanation.surface: A woman tempted to eat a giant burger after dinner finds it comforting.
explanation.walkthrough: A Whopper is a Burger King burger, but here it is a tall tale. The R goes first although its words come last, as 'after' allows.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve someone is to ease their distress, to comfort them.

clue.text: Pressure on games at Wimbledon determined in advance

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for pressure
re means on or concerning, as in a memo
in tennis, a set is a group of games

explanation.surface: A tennis player feels the pressure of matches at Wimbledon decided beforehand.
explanation.definitionFit: Something preset has been fixed or arranged ahead of time, so it is settled before the event.

clue.text: Halo with gravitational attraction can feature

parts.note: a halo is a ring of light
gravity is a pull between masses

explanation.surface: A physicist wonders whether a planetary ring with its gravity can be featured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb meaning is able to; it is a drinks tin, and the answer is one of its parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The tab you lift to open a drinks tin is a standard part of the container's design.

clue.text: Moscow's tyrant: run to stop believer in that barbarian

indicators.note: a plug stops a hole by going into it, so this letter is put inside the rearranged phrase
barbarian means wild and uncivilised, so the letters before it are treated roughly into a new order

parts.note: the three words used letter for letter as material to rearrange
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A Muscovite despot is told to suppress anyone believing in a particular savage.
explanation.walkthrough: The fourteen letters of 'believer in that' rearrange to the name with only one R; the R from 'run' is slipped in to make the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan IV, Grand Prince of Moscow and first Tsar of Russia, was notorious for his cruelty and is the archetypal Russian despot.

clue.text: Fan of Spock or Kirk regularly there, excited

indicators.note: excited means agitated, so the gathered letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the word that follows is kept

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A Star Trek devotee gets excited whenever Spock or Captain Kirk is on screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' looks as if it governs Kirk, but Kirk is used whole and only 'there' is thinned out.
explanation.definitionFit: Trekkie is the nickname for an enthusiast of Star Trek, the series in which Spock appears.

clue.text: Eighteen holes — drinks at nineteenth?
Unassailable chorizo perhaps served up by Puck?

parts.note: Puck is the mischievous sprite in A Midsummer Night's Dream, a little devil

indicators.note: served up in a down clue means the item is brought upward, so its letters run from bottom to top

parts.note: chorizo is a Spanish sausage, jokily rendered as Spanish el plus banger

explanation.surface: A spicy sausage is offered by Puck, who cannot be resisted.
explanation.walkthrough: Banger is British slang for sausage, and a Spanish one is playfully 'el banger'; that phrase reads upward beside IMP.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortress that is impregnable cannot be taken, so it is proof against attack.

clue.text: Poor here soon displaced

indicators.note: displaced letters have been moved out of their positions into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the two words used letter for letter as material

explanation.surface: Impoverished people here will soon be forced out of their homes.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-horse town or outfit is small, backward and inferior, so the adjective means poor in quality.

clue.text: Sailor in bunk to sleep as birds do

indicators.note: in places the sailor's abbreviation inside the word for nonsense

parts.note: bunk is nonsense, rubbish, rot
OS is an Ordinary Seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor climbs into his bunk to sleep like a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Bunk looks like a sailor's bed; it is short for bunkum, meaning nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds roost when they settle on a perch for the night, their equivalent of sleeping.

clue.text: Official in uniform quietly sucked into bog

parts.note: U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: whatever is sucked into a marsh ends up inside it, so one letter goes into the bog's word

parts.note: a mire is a bog or swamp
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: An official in uniform is quietly sucked down into a marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: U stands before MIRE, and P is pushed inside MIRE after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An umpire is the official who enforces the rules in cricket, tennis and other sports.

clue.text: Staggered about etc when drunk returned to office

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for staggered goes around the other letters

parts.note: to reel is to stagger

indicators.note: drunk letters lurch out of line into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as material

explanation.surface: A politician stumbled about drunk after being voted back in.
explanation.definitionFit: Being re-elected means voters have returned you to the post you held.

clue.text: Atomic City — very good composition
Old boy in defamation where case dropped by us?

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, so dropping it strips the first and last letters

parts.note: calumny is a false and slanderous statement
taken as written

explanation.surface: A former pupil is caught up in a libel case that we decided to drop.
explanation.walkthrough: Case looks like a lawsuit; it is the outer letters C and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: An old boy is a former pupil of a school, and an alumnus is a former student.

clue.text: Dish of Greek weed (not with bananas)

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the remaining letters go wildly out of order
not with tells you to drop the abbreviation for with from the material

parts.note: the two words as letter material
W is the standard abbreviation for with, here removed

explanation.surface: A recipe for a Greek dish made from some wild plant, with the bananas left out.
explanation.walkthrough: Bananas looks like a fruit missing from the dish, but it is the scrambling signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Kedgeree is an Anglo-Indian dish of rice, smoked fish and boiled eggs, often eaten at breakfast.

clue.text: Hidden from public scrutiny with summer over?

definitions.text: Hidden from public scrutiny with summer over?

parts.note: surface reading: kept secret, sold illicitly, out of sight
setter's reading: a summer is one who does sums, another word for someone who tallies figures, and that person is placed above you

explanation.surface: Something kept out of the public eye now that the holiday season has ended.
explanation.walkthrough: Summer looks like the season; read it as sum-mer, one who adds things up, and if such a person is over you, you are beneath them.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods sold covertly or illegally are passed below the shop's serving surface, hence the idiom for secret dealings.

clue.text: Perhaps pointer before noon reverses belief

parts.note: a pointer is a breed of gun dog, perhaps signalling an example

indicators.note: reverses turns the time abbreviation back to front

parts.note: am, ante meridiem, is the time before noon

explanation.surface: A gundog turning back before midday seems to change its mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Before noon gives AM, which is then turned round and placed after the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogma is a firmly held belief or doctrine laid down as true.

clue.text: Relationship over, call for sailor's attention?

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the call that follows is read backwards

parts.note: Oi, tar! is how you might shout for a sailor, tar being slang for a seaman

explanation.surface: A love affair ends; someone shouts for a sailor to look their way.
explanation.walkthrough: Over looks like the end of a romance; it reverses 'Oi, tar!'. Oi is a British call to get attention.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio expresses the quantitative relation between two amounts, so it is a mathematical relationship.

clue.text: Yank in paradise not initially expelled

indicators.note: expelled means thrown out, so that letter is removed from the word for paradise

parts.note: heaven is paradise

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An American in heaven, until he is thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: Yank looks like an American; it is a verb, a hard pull.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave is to pull or haul with great effort, just as to yank is to tug sharply.

clue.text: How swindler is selected for side? Not in the normal way

definitions.text: How swindler is selected for side?
definitions.meaning: first meaning: take the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of swindler and you get side

explanation.surface: A crook is picked for the team by some irregular process.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads like team selection; it is a riddle about which letters of 'swindler' spell 'side'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something strangely is doing it peculiarly, and selecting the odd-numbered letters is a literal sense too.

clue.text: Beer in the evening for silent winger?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, whimsically split: a jar (pint of beer) taken at night
second meaning: a nocturnal bird whose soft plumage lets it fly without a sound

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a pint at night would suit a quiet footballer on the flank.
explanation.walkthrough: A jar is British slang for a glass of beer. Winger suggests a football position; it means a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The nightjar is a dusk-feeding bird with notably soft, silent flight, and the word splits into night plus slang for a pint.

clue.text: Scots pass around heavy stick, which is deliberate

indicators.note: around places the first item on both sides of the second, wrapping it

parts.note: in Scots, dee is the word for die, to pass away
a bat is a heavy club or stick

explanation.surface: Scottish players hand a heavy staff about, perhaps in a Highland game.
explanation.walkthrough: Pass looks like handing something on or a mountain route; it is pass as in pass away, and Scots dialect says dee for die.
explanation.definitionFit: To debate a question is to deliberate over it, weighing arguments for and against.

clue.text: Made gloomy broadcast, tricked into it

indicators.note: into it puts the second word inside the first one, the 'it' pointing back to that word

parts.note: to broadcast seed is to scatter it, to sow it
to be had is to be tricked or fooled

explanation.surface: A gloomy programme went out on air after someone was conned into making it.
explanation.walkthrough: Broadcast looks like radio or TV; it is the farming sense, scattering seed by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shadowed has been darkened or cast into shade, so made gloomy.

clue.text: Bond returns: gives way under pressure?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the interest income earned on bonds, as a plural noun
second meaning: a verb, collapses or submits when pushed

explanation.surface: A financial headline: bond prices bounce back, then buckle under strain.
explanation.walkthrough: Returns looks like a verb, as if James Bond comes back; it is a noun, the income investors get.
explanation.definitionFit: The yield of a bond is its rate of return, and to yield is also to give in or bend under force.
